about: Yes Honey is a crude two-character drawing: on the left a smiling woman with long brown hair and a red sweater sits with her hands calmly folded, and on the right a hollow-eyed, wrinkled Wojak stares back like a man who gave up arguing years ago. She states something, he agrees. The humor comes from how little resistance he puts up. Whatever she says, sensible or absurd, he answers with a flat "yes honey", and his exhausted face tells you he has said it thousands of times. It is a gentle roast of anyone who agrees with a partner, boss, client or product owner just to keep the peace.
usage:
The top box is her line: a request, a decree or a confident opinion. The bottom box is his answer, which is almost always just "yes honey". Keep the wording lowercase-feeling and plain so the deadpan works.

The joke lands hardest when the request is unreasonable but delivered with total calm, like moving the deadline up or rewriting a working app from scratch. You can also flip it to tech or hobby culture, where a tool, a framework or a game developer plays the woman and the community plays the tired Wojak.
ideas: we should rewrite it in rust
you will buy the battle pass again
we're spending christmas at my parents' this year
the meeting could have been an email but we're doing it anyway
you will accept the new terms of service
your group project partner: I'll do the slides, you do everything else
